claim.supported_scope: Qualified two-group MICOM v4 Steps 1-3 coupled to deterministic two-tailed permutation comparisons of PLS paths, outer loadings, and outer weights under one shared fixed indexed partition plan with exactly-once no-retry accounting.
claim.estimand: Compositional correlation, pooled-score mean and log-variance differences, and two-group parameter differences under a canonical seeded label-permutation reference distribution.
assumptions: Exactly two selected groups use the same supported PLS model, coding, preprocessing, path weighting, and listwise case treatment.
The researcher confirms MICOM Step 1 semantic and configural conditions.
Permutation streams preserve group sizes and successful group solutions are sign-aligned to the pooled reference.
exclusions: More than two simultaneous groups, parametric or bootstrap MGA, one-tailed MGA, omnibus tests, and multiplicity correction are excluded.
Case weights, interactions, higher-order models, covariance-only input, and consistent PLS variants are excluded.
MICOM does not prove semantic equivalence, validity, causality, or representativeness.
warnings: Interpret an MGA difference only after establishing at least partial invariance for the relevant composite.
Historical v1-v3 combined results remain readable under their original identities but cannot be appended as v4 evidence.
Every requested v4 partition is attempted once; failed fits remain in the typed shared ledger and are never retried or replaced.

references.citation: Henseler, Ringle, and Sarstedt (2016), Testing Measurement Invariance of Composites Using Partial Least Squares
Independent fixed-plan MICOM and permutation-MGA v4 oracle

simulations.design: Independent numerical A/B and B/A executions plus exhaustive small finite partitions and varied seeded streams.
simulations.seed_policy: Canonical unordered group pool with exact complemented labels for the reverse direction.
simulations.acceptance_rule: All finite-plan checks pass exactly and the 5,000-permutation independent calculation matches QuickPLS within 1e-6.

simulations.design: Exchangeable two-group null scenarios for paths, loadings, and weights.
simulations.seed_policy: Frozen indexed scenario and canonical permutation streams.
simulations.acceptance_rule: The preregistered interval contains 0.05, its upper bound is at most 0.065, and every failed fit remains accounted for.

boundaries.case: A group is too small or a supported-model permutation fit fails.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Setup is blocked or the failed indexed attempt is retained exactly once with a stable typed reason; it is never replaced.

boundaries.case: More than two groups, unsupported settings, or missing configural confirmation are requested.
Group A and B are exchanged consistently.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Signed differences reverse exactly; two-tailed p values, failed counts, and MICOM decisions remain equal.

boundaries.case: The same data, seed, and recipe use different supported worker counts.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Permutation assignments, successful fits, ordering, and analytical payload are exactly equal.

boundaries.case: Identity, direction, counts, decisions, p values, or checksums change.
boundaries.expected_behavior: Strict project validation rejects the archive.

tamper_tests.expected_behavior: Reject current evidence relabeled as another version.
Reject invalid counts, directions, values, identities, ledgers, digests, decisions, or probability lattices.
Never reinterpret v1-v3 output as v4 evidence.

persistence.legacy_policy: v1-v3 bundles remain archive-readable under their exact historical identities and cannot be appended as v4 evidence.

native.gui_cli_parity_rule: Identical data, settings, seed, and workers produce the exact same analytical payload apart from timestamps.
accessibility_rules: Direction, decisions, probabilities, warnings, and failures do not rely on color alone.
